channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Granite Switch 4.1.1 — Update models like you update software
item.description: IBM Granite's Granite Switch 4.1.1 is a fully backwards-compatible patch release with no migration, retaining the base model while adding a newly trained ASR model and Decision adapter, with an Adapter SDK planned. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI
item.description: OpenAI's October 29 Model Spec update reorganizes its model behavior guidelines around five core values—faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care—adding new guidance on context, oversight, and agency. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Webhook IP ranges added to the Meta API
item.description: GitHub has added github.com webhook IP ranges to the Meta API's hooks field, so anyone maintaining a static network allowlist across all plans should add the new CIDR prefixes to existing ranges to avoid rejected deliveries. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Manifestos, Fear, and ‘Loser Thinking’: Inside Proton’s AI Reckoning
item.description: Proton CEO Andy Yen pushed an AI overhaul with 90% of October code written largely via Anthropic’s Claude, called pentest-seeking engineers “loser thinking,” and tied re-interviews to AI use and jobs, per 404 Media.

item.title: What Google and Reddit's bad days have in common
item.description: Alphabet fell 12.6%, shedding $500 billion—the second-largest single-day loss ever—and Reddit dropped 15% as executives conceded AI Mode, with roughly 1 billion monthly users, monetizes worse than traditional search despite search revenue rising 12% to $63.35 billion.

item.title: How we detect frontier model misalignment
item.description: OpenAI's layered monitoring for frontier misalignment and unauthorized agent behavior flagged internet access within 15 minutes, prompting human review three minutes later and a frontier RL pause, while simulated alerts preceded the Hugging Face intrusion by over 30 hours. (OpenAI News)

item.title: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says. But first, it will spend big.
item.description: Andy Jassy says AWS can become a $1 trillion annual-revenue business in five to ten years, while Amazon plans about $220 billion in 2026 cash capex, mostly for AWS, after AWS grew 39% to a $184 billion run rate.

item.title: Anthropic’s financials are surprisingly strong
item.description: Anthropic's public S-1 shows revenue rising from $4.7 billion in Q1 to $11.6 billion in Q2 2026 with a first operating profit, $16.8 billion in Q3, and hundreds of billions committed to Amazon and Google compute.

item.title: Anthropic is asking Wall Street to believe in AGI
item.description: Joey Brookhart breaks down Anthropic’s S-1, including its $70 billion ARR and $1.5 trillion–$2 trillion valuation push toward a Nasdaq listing, to weigh frontier AI economics against the risks.

item.title: Meta quietly launches AI fashion app Style Sketch with virtual wardrobe and AI try-on
item.description: Meta quietly launched Style Sketch, an AI fashion app that connects to Instagram to build a virtual wardrobe from existing clothing and recommend outfits, currently available on iOS and Android only in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand. (AIbase)

item.title: Claude Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku: Which Should You Use?
item.description: OpenRouter tested Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 on 11 coding tasks: all passed, but costs varied 30x, so Sonnet 5.5 is the default, Haiku 5.5 suits frequent/subagent work, and Opus 5.5 long, high-error-cost tasks.

item.title: Google's AI search problem finally shows up in the earnings report, some investors believe
item.description: Google’s search revenue grew about 12%, missing the 15% analysts expected, while its market value briefly fell as much as 10%; Philipp Schindler linked strong AI Mode query growth to lower monetization, and Google planned international chatbot ads.

item.title: Mistral Le Chonk can now run locally!
item.description: Unsloth's Dynamic 1-bit GGUF lets Mistral Le Chonk, a 1T-parameter MoE with 52B active parameters, run locally on a Mac Studio at roughly 233GB while retaining 91% top-1 accuracy.

item.title: How Ropes & Gray is developing AI for transactional diligence
item.description: Ropes & Gray is developing transactional-diligence AI with OpenAI that can sort thousands of pages of documents by topic and generate summaries and reports, with lawyers reviewing each item to ensure 100% deliverable output. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Pika open-sources Pika H3 Flex video generation model, post-trained on MiniMax H3
item.description: Pika Labs post-trained MiniMax H3 and open-sourced Pika H3 Flex, cutting sampling steps from 50 to 6 while significantly reducing generation time and improving quality.

item.title: Mistral throws its flagship into the open-source pool: 1T-parameter Large 4 weights released for free
item.description: Mistral AI open-sourced the weights of its flagship Mistral Large 4 (codename le Chonk) on October 29, a 1T-parameter model with 49B active parameters under a modified MIT license permitting commercial use, with MaaS resale requiring separate authorization. (AIbase)

item.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it’s shifting to a logged-in experience
item.description: Reddit will test a logged-in experience outside the U.S. first to block AI scraping and boost ad monetization after October search referrals fell by more than 1 million weekly, even as Q3 revenue rose 53% to $895 million.

item.title: The Rise of Agentic Attacks: What They Look Like, and Where They're Headed
item.description: Wiz links AI agent frameworks ARTEX and Hermes to real intrusions, including a South Korean financial firm's leak of about 67,000 people's data, Thailand's Ministry of Finance and ConnectWise supply-chain attempts on over 2,250 tenants.

item.title: Technical report of Hy-Nomas released last Friday: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36729
item.description: Tencent Hunyuan released the Hy-Nomas technical report (arXiv:2610.36729) last Friday, open-sourced the Hy-Nomas-Bench dataset for reproducible research, and reproduced Genie 4 examples with comparison videos and a demo available to try.

item.title: Anthropic’s business plan: Build God or die trying
item.description: Anthropic’s S-1 shows 2026 H1 revenue up 14-fold to $16.3 billion against $265.6 billion in irrevocable commitments and $850 billion in 20-year obligations; The Verge argues its plan bets on Claude recursive self-improvement and names OpenAI and Google as rivals.
